notes: PX-2 native full-tile fp8 mainloop for d_gemm_w8a8/d_gemm_glu_w8a8: fp8 K-tile deepened BK 32->64 (two m16n8k32 e4m3 mmas per K-tile => half the __syncthreads/cp.async cadence per K element, same smem bytes as bf16's 32-deep tile) + fp8-native CuTe Swizzle<3,4,3> (pgm_sw8) on the plain-uint32 fp8 frag reads, applied identically on cp.async store and read (pure address bijection => oracle bit-identical). Reuses T8's two-scale epilogue and the T3 cp.async ring unchanged; only tile shape/K-depth/swizzle changed. Measurement harness = gemma4_sm120_chat (chunked prefill, PLOW_PREFILL=1 PLOW_UNISEG=1), same w8a8 pkt run under the T8 vs PX-2 cubin; block-0 per-op body cycles via PLOW_NV_TRACE=1 (trace_reduce.py). bf16 leg is the same harness on a bf16 pkt. op33=GEMM_FP8, op36=GEMM_GLU_FP8, op32=QUANT_FP8.

isolated_gemm_bench_negative.note: experiments/px2_gemm_bench.cu times the GEMM kernel STANDALONE (188 blocks, real gemma-12B projection shapes). There PX-2 is 3-10% SLOWER than T8 (w8a8/bf16 ratio 0.50-0.54 vs T8's 0.46-0.52); both already ~2x bf16. The standalone GEMM runs at higher occupancy so BK=32's extra syncs are hidden and BK=64's bigger cp.async stages hurt. The win is ONLY visible in the occ-1 megakernel (240 regs, 81 KiB smem, 1 block/SM) where the cp.async/sync cadence binds — exactly the 'bf16 cadence' PX-2 targets. Recorded so the in-context win is not mistaken for a standalone-kernel property.
isolated_gemm_bench_negative.swizzle_ab: PX-2 with swizzle beats PX-2 without (w8a8/bf16 0.50-0.54 vs 0.54-0.58) in the same standalone bench — the fp8 Swizzle<3,4,3> does reduce the plain-read bank conflict.
